main_issue: Where to hold the farewell lunch, since the chosen Korean BBQ doesn't work for three of them, and whether to ask the leaver for a second choice or find an alternative themselves (Peranakan).

A-B.evidence: B initially wanted to keep Korean BBQ (6) while A wanted another place (5); later B agrees with A (14), though A briefly flipped to asking her (17) and B opposed (18); end: PeraMakan, A calls (23).

A-C.evidence: Both said Korean BBQ doesn't work (5, 7); C accepts Peranakan (15) and A calls the restaurant (23). They never addressed each other directly.

A-D.evidence: A agrees with D's coeliac concern (5) and with the soy point (17), and thanks D for the find (21, 23); A briefly takes up D's ask-her idea (17), then drops it for PeraMakan (23).

B-C.evidence: C says it won't work (7, 9); B concedes (8, 10); both go along with calling a Peranakan place near the office (15, 18, 19).

B-D.evidence: B concedes Korean BBQ is too risky for D (10); B rejects D's ask-her idea (18) but accepts D's PeraMakan find (22) and the gluten-free check.

C-D.evidence: C backs the safety concern for D (9) and wants a nearby place (19); D finds one five minutes away (22).
